research_mode: official ONS and Office for Statistics Regulation sources only; recording-quality governance, inspection, rule-change, survey-design and uncertainty gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: National registrar advice platform
verified_claims: force registrars can seek advice from the National Crime Registrar
queries and answers are shared on a Police Digital Service knowledge platform
limitations: advice availability does not prove uniform implementation

sources.name: 2023 principal crime rule
verified_claims: the 2023 review reintroduced the principal crime rule so generally only the most serious crime is recorded for a multi-offence incident
limitations: police may investigate all disclosed offences even when not all are statistically recorded

sources.name: Principal-rule exceptions
verified_claims: modern-slavery offences and passport-application fraud remain exempt from the reintroduced principal crime rule

sources.name: Section 5 public-order status
verified_claims: the 2023 review made section 5 Public Order Act 1986 offences non-notifiable
limitations: the rule change creates a break in recorded totals

sources.name: Domestic-abuse nuance risk
verified_claims: some forces warned that recording only one crime per incident may lose nuance in domestic-abuse offending patterns
limitations: this is a quality concern, not a quantified national adjustment

sources.name: Counting-rule trend ambiguity
verified_claims: regular counting-rule changes make it difficult to distinguish genuine crime change from recording-practice change
limitations: time-series interpretation must preserve rule-version metadata

sources.name: CSEW long-term trend role
verified_claims: CSEW estimates are not affected by police counting-rule changes and are more reliable for long-term trends in covered crime
limitations: CSEW excludes crimes and populations outside its survey scope

sources.name: Risk-averse over-recording
verified_claims: inspection pressure can encourage a risk-averse record-everything approach that increases over-recording
limitations: higher recording accuracy does not rule out over-recording

sources.name: Crime cancellation evidence rule
verified_claims: a recorded crime remains a crime unless additional verifiable information proves it did not happen
limitations: cancellation thresholds can affect recorded volumes

sources.name: Over-recording-sensitive offence types
verified_claims: stakeholders reported over-recording as more common for stalking and harassment, domestic abuse and malicious communications
limitations: the review did not quantify national over-recording by offence

sources.name: Over-recording grading gap
verified_claims: HMICFRS examines over-recording but those findings do not influence the overall crime-data-integrity grading
forces are penalised for under-recording, not over-recording
limitations: a high grade must not be interpreted as proof of no over-recording

sources.name: Home Office oversight risk
verified_claims: OSR considers insufficient Home Office oversight a significant risk to the quality of police-recorded-crime statistics
limitations: the recommendation concerns system assurance, not an offence estimate

sources.name: QAAD consistency plan
verified_claims: OSR recommends a detailed Home Office plan for consistent force quality assurance using the QAAD framework
limitations: the framework guides assurance and does not itself certify each record

sources.name: IT-system strengths and limitations
verified_claims: Home Office should understand strengths and limitations of different force crime-recording IT systems and their data-quality effects
limitations: system variation remains a comparability constraint

sources.name: ONS quality disclosure scope
verified_claims: ONS should publish information on force quality assurance, IT-system strengths and limitations, and improvements since 2014
limitations: published disclosure supports interpretation but does not correct source data
